name: Vina Falls
shortDescription: A dramatic 40m waterfall near Ngaoundéré.
fullDescription: Located about 15 km from Ngaoundéré, the Vina River plunges roughly 40 meters into a natural rock amphitheater, forming one of the Adamawa region's most striking natural sights.
funFact: The falls form a distinctive arc shape as the water cascades over the rock formation.

name: Lamido's Palace of Ngaoundéré
shortDescription: Traditional palace of the Fulani Lamido (ruler).
fullDescription: This palace showcases traditional Fulani architecture and remains the ceremonial seat of the Lamido, the traditional ruler of Ngaoundéré.
funFact: The palace's decorated walls illustrate centuries-old Fulani architectural traditions.

name: National Museum of Yaoundé
shortDescription: Cameroon's national collection of art and history.
fullDescription: Housed in a former presidential palace, this museum showcases artifacts, traditional art, and exhibits spanning Cameroon's diverse cultural history.
funFact: The building itself was once the official residence of Cameroon's first president.

name: Reunification Monument
shortDescription: Iconic monument marking Cameroon's 1961 reunification.
fullDescription: This landmark sculpture in Yaoundé commemorates the 1961 reunification of French and British Cameroon into a single nation.
funFact: The monument's spiraling design symbolizes the two territories coming together as one.

name: Dja Faunal Reserve
shortDescription: UNESCO-listed rainforest reserve, one of Africa's largest and best-protected.
fullDescription: Almost entirely surrounded by the Dja River, this reserve protects vast untouched rainforest and is home to gorillas, chimpanzees, and forest elephants.
funFact: Over 90% of the reserve remains undisturbed primary rainforest.
openingHours: Guided tours only, arrange in advance

name: Lobéké National Park
shortDescription: Remote rainforest park known for forest elephants and lowland gorillas.
fullDescription: Part of the Sangha Trinational conservation complex, Lobéké protects dense rainforest and forest clearings (bais) where wildlife gathers.
funFact: Lobéké's forest clearings let visitors observe forest elephants and gorillas in open view — rare for rainforest terrain.
openingHours: Guided tours only, arrange in advance

name: Waza National Park
shortDescription: Cameroon's premier safari destination.
fullDescription: One of Central Africa's best wildlife parks, Waza is home to elephants, lions, giraffes, and hundreds of bird species across open savanna.
funFact: Waza is not a zoo — animals roam freely across the savanna, making it a true wilderness safari experience.

name: Rhumsiki Peak
shortDescription: Dramatic volcanic rock spire in the Mandara Mountains.
fullDescription: This iconic volcanic plug rises sharply from the surrounding Kapsiki plateau, surrounded by traditional villages and stunning sunset views.
funFact: Rhumsiki's jagged volcanic landscape has made it one of Cameroon's most photographed natural sites.

name: Douala Maritime Museum
shortDescription: Museum dedicated to Cameroon's seafaring and port history.
fullDescription: Located in the historic Bonanjo district, this museum traces Douala's evolution as a major port city through artifacts, models, and exhibits on maritime trade.
funFact: The museum includes a pirogue (canoe) simulator that lets visitors experience traditional local boating.

name: Douala-Edéa Wildlife Reserve
shortDescription: Mangrove and forest reserve near Douala.
fullDescription: Covering roughly 160,000 hectares, this reserve protects mangrove wetlands and rainforest, home to elephants, primates, and sea turtles.
funFact: The reserve's mangroves provide a rare habitat for manatees along Cameroon's coast.
openingHours: Guided tours only, arrange in advance

name: Benoué National Park
shortDescription: Savanna park along the Benoue River.
fullDescription: One of Cameroon's key protected areas, home to lions, elephants, hippos, and hundreds of bird species along the Benoue River floodplains.
funFact: The park is named after the Benoue River, a major tributary that eventually joins the Niger River in Nigeria.

name: Rey Bouba Palace
shortDescription: Historic royal palace of the Lamido of Rey Bouba.
fullDescription: One of northern Cameroon's most important traditional palaces, seat of the powerful Lamido (traditional ruler) of Rey Bouba.
funFact: Rey Bouba's Lamidat is one of the oldest and most influential traditional Fulani kingdoms in the region.

name: Bamenda Ring Road
shortDescription: Scenic 367 km highland loop through villages and volcanic lakes.
fullDescription: This famous circuit winds through the Northwest's grassfields, passing waterfalls, crater lakes, and traditional villages along the way.
funFact: The Ring Road passes near several volcanic crater lakes formed by the region's ancient volcanic activity.
openingHours: Accessible daily, best in dry season

name: Bafut Palace
shortDescription: Traditional palace of the Fon (king) of Bafut.
fullDescription: This historic royal compound is the seat of the Fon of Bafut, featuring traditional architecture and a small museum of royal artifacts.
funFact: Bafut's traditional kingdom structure has remained largely intact for centuries.

name: Lobé Falls
shortDescription: Rare waterfall that flows directly into the ocean.
fullDescription: Located just outside Kribi, the Lobé River cascades directly into the Atlantic Ocean — one of very few waterfalls in the world to do so.
funFact: Local Batanga fishermen still paddle traditional canoes right up to the base of the falls.

name: Campo Ma'an National Park
shortDescription: Rainforest park near the coast, rich in biodiversity.
fullDescription: This park protects dense equatorial rainforest along Cameroon's southern coast, home to gorillas, forest elephants, and over 300 bird species.
funFact: Campo Ma'an is one of the most biodiverse protected areas in Central Africa.
openingHours: Guided tours only, arrange in advance

name: Mount Cameroon
shortDescription: West Africa's highest peak and an active volcano.
fullDescription: Standing at 4,040 m, Mount Cameroon is a major trekking destination, with routes taking climbers through rainforest, grassland, and volcanic terrain to the summit.
funFact: Mount Cameroon is one of Africa's most active volcanoes, with its most recent eruption in 2000.
openingHours: Guided treks, register in Buea before climbing

name: Limbe Botanic Garden
shortDescription: One of Africa's oldest botanical gardens.
fullDescription: Founded in 1892, this coastal garden showcases hundreds of tropical plant species along the Atlantic shoreline.
funFact: The garden was originally established by German colonial botanists in the 19th century.

name: Foumban Royal Palace
shortDescription: Historic palace and museum of the Bamoun Kingdom.
fullDescription: Home to generations of Bamoun kings (Sultans), this palace complex includes a museum displaying royal artifacts, art, and centuries of Bamoun history.
funFact: The Bamoun Kingdom developed its own writing script in the early 20th century, still preserved in the palace archives.

name: Bandjoun Chefferie
shortDescription: Traditional Bamileke royal chiefdom and museum.
fullDescription: This royal compound showcases Bamileke traditional architecture, wood carvings, and a museum preserving the chiefdom's cultural heritage.
funFact: The chiefdom's main hall features intricately carved wooden pillars, a hallmark of Bamileke craftsmanship.
